title: Virata: the year in disguise
hook: a bundle tied high in a shami tree near the cremation ground, and nobody wants to go near it

segments.voice: Yesterday: Virata, the king whose court will hide them, and five brothers and a queen choosing who to be. Your line was every disguise is built from something real.
screen: `VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.` · `EVERY DISGUISE BUILT ON A REAL SKILL.`

segments.voice: A shami tree stands near a cremation ground outside King Virata's city. Thick branches, hard to climb, and a place people would rather walk past. Nakula climbs it. He ties a long bundle high in the branches, wrapped tight so the rain won't reach it. Inside is luggage that could end the whole disguise: Arjuna's bow, the Gandiva, and the brothers' other weapons. A wandering cook can't carry a bow every warrior knows on sight. So the weapons stay behind.
screen: `A SHAMI TREE BY THE CREMATION GROUND.` → `NAKULA CLIMBS.` → `THE WEAPONS STAY BEHIND.`

segments.voice: The text adds a detail that's half clever, half grim. To keep curious people away, the brothers tie a dead body to the tree as well, and tell passing herdsmen it's an old family custom, a mother's body hung there by tradition. Nobody climbs a tree like that. Then they enter the city one at a time, so no one sees five strong men arrive together. Yudhishthira comes first, with dice wrapped in cloth under his arm, and King Virata takes to him at once and makes him his companion. Bhima arrives with a cook's ladle and a knife. Arjuna comes in women's ornaments and asks to teach dance. Nakula and Sahadeva go to the stables and the herds. Draupadi walks the streets in a single worn cloth until Queen Sudeshna sees her from a terrace and calls her up. The queen hesitates. You're too beautiful, she says; the king will look at you. Draupadi answers with a story of her own: she has husbands, Gandharvas, heavenly beings who guard her unseen and will punish anyone who troubles her. It's a disguise inside the disguise, and it's also true. Her husbands really are watching over her, from the kitchen, the stables and the dice table. The heroes leave their weapons in a tree and their names at the gate, and keep only themselves.
screen: `A BODY TO KEEP PEOPLE AWAY` · `ARRIVING ONE AT A TIME` · `THE QUEEN'S WORRY` · then, large: `HIDDEN GANDHARVA HUSBANDS`

segments.voice: If something you carry every day is near you, a phone, keys, a bag, set it down out of reach and sit comfortably. Notice the small pull to check it and let that pull be there, then breathe in with empty hands and ask quietly what's left when the familiar things are put away for a while. If you pray, you can rest in that question in your prayer.
Virata. The king who welcomes a dice player, a cook, a dance teacher, two herders and a maid, never guessing who they are.
Your line: keep only themselves. No bow, no names, just who they were. That's day eight hundred eight.

chat.says: Why did the Pandavas hide their weapons in a tree before entering the city?
options: A cook or a dance teacher can't carry weapons every warrior knows on sight.
They had promised Dharma never to use weapons again after the lake.
King Virata banned all weapons inside his city during that year.
chat.meaning: Arjuna's bow, the Gandiva, would give them away. They left their weapons in the shami tree and walked in with nothing but themselves.

shami.meaning: a hardy tree; the Pandavas hide their weapons in one

Gandiva.meaning: Arjuna's bow, known to every warrior on sight

Sudeshna.meaning: King Virata's queen, who takes Draupadi on as a maid

Gandharvas.meaning: heavenly beings; Draupadi says hers guard her unseen

Virata.meaning: king of the Matsyas, in whose court the Pandavas hide

recall: a tree whose name means without sorrow
